# API keys

The commands `mt help` lists under API keys. More in [Your API key](../../../get-started/2-api-key.md).

In a terminal, type `mt` and then the command. In the interactive shell and the cloud shell, type the command on
its own. `mt help <command>` shows the same details in your terminal.

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`api-key-create`](#api-key-create) | Create an API key and show how to use it, once (needs a sign-in with an email address and password, not an API key) |
| [`api-key-delete`](#api-key-delete) | Disable one of your API keys, so it no longer signs in (needs a sign-in with an email address and password, not an API key) |
| [`api-key-list`](#api-key-list) | List your API keys: name, dates and id, never the secret (needs a sign-in with an email address and password, not an API key) |

## api-key-create

Create an API key and show how to use it, once (needs a sign-in with an email address and password, not an API key).

```text
mt api-key-create <name> [options]
```

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `<name>` | text | yes |  | A name for the key, unique among your keys |

| Option | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--expires-days <number>` | whole number |  |  | Days until the key expires (default: it never expires) |

## api-key-delete

Disable one of your API keys, so it no longer signs in (needs a sign-in with an email address and password, not an API key).

```text
mt api-key-delete <id>
```

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `<id>` | id | yes |  | The key's own id, as api-key-list shows it (not the user id the key signs in with) |

## api-key-list

List your API keys: name, dates and id, never the secret (needs a sign-in with an email address and password, not an API key).

```text
mt api-key-list
```
